meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 14: MCP Registry (multi-select)
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: Which statements about what the registry does NOT do are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: It does not allow closed-source servers to be listed
It does not accept servers that are only reachable on private networks
It does not support remote servers, only installable packages
It does not perform its own security scanning of server code
It is not designed to be self-hosted from the official codebase

questions.explanation: Private servers are out of scope, scanning is delegated to package registries and aggregators, and the maintainers do not support self-hosting the official codebase. Closed-source servers are fine as long as installation or access is public, and remote servers are supported.

questions.question: Which steps belong to publishing a server to the official registry? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Upload the server's source archive to the registry for scanning
Describe the server in server.json with a reverse-DNS name
Authenticate the namespace with mcp-publisher login (GitHub, DNS or HTTP)
Add the ownership marker for the package type to the published package
Register a webhook so the registry can health-check the remote server

questions.explanation: Publishing is metadata plus proof: a server.json with a namespaced name, namespace authentication, and a package-side ownership marker. The registry never hosts source, and it does not health-check servers.

questions.question: Which statements about proving ownership across package ecosystems are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: PyPI and NuGet packages carry a mcp-name: line in the README
Cargo crates need the marker in visible text, because crates.io strips HTML comments
npm packages carry the claim in a mcpName field in package.json
MCPB packages are verified by the registry, which recomputes fileSha256 on upload
OCI images are verified by the registry, which pulls and inspects every tag

questions.explanation: The markers differ per ecosystem, and the crates.io rule follows from it stripping HTML comments, so a hidden marker would never be seen. The fileSha256 on an MCPB entry is verified by the installing client, not by the registry.
